rows.letter:
To the Road Authority

Subject: Request for safety improvement at Lake View Road crossing

Dear Sir/Madam,

We recorded activity at Lake View Road crossing for 17.9 minutes (1074.0 s). In that time we counted 30 crossings and 14 vehicles. The 85th percentile speed was 45.5 km/h.

Of 30 crossings, 4 of 30 (1 in 7.5) had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3.0 s of the person and 2 of 30 (1 in 15) within 1.5 s. If this recording is typical, the exact 95% ranges are 3.8-30.7% and 0.8-22.1% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 1.1-10.2 and 0.2-7.2 people in a recording this long (Poisson). There was 1 serious near-miss where the person was first, 3 where the vehicle was first, and 0 where both were at once.

One serious near-miss involved a motorcycle at 44.9 km/h with 1.4 s between the person and vehicle. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk would be 5.4% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).

Another serious near-miss involved a bus at 26.8 km/h with 1.0 s between the person and vehicle. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk would be 1.1%.

One close pass involved a car at 21.3 km/h with 2.0 s between the person and vehicle. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk would be 0.0%.

Another close pass involved a bus at 23.4 km/h with 2.3 s between the person and vehicle. For an adult hit by a car front at that speed the death risk would be 0.0%.

For context, PV² was 0.0 x 10^8, from 101 pedestrians and 47 moving vehicles an hour scaled from 17.9 minutes of video, noting a formal check counts the full peak hour and broken tracks can count 1.3x.

52.7% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 1 such gap and a longest gap of 11.4 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request that you install a raised zebra crossing with speed table at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and provide priority for people crossing.

We are happy to share the video and Crossing Watch measurements (SAM tracking, road-plane geometry, post-encroachment time) for your review.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal
The Principal will add approval name and date on signing.

Dear Sir or Madam,

Re: Safety at Brook Street crossing

We write on behalf of our school about the crossing outside it. A video survey of 7.3 minutes (438.0 s) recorded 3 pedestrian crossings and 6 moving vehicles, with an 85th percentile speed of 57.4 km/h.

Of 3 crossings, 3 had a moving vehicle through the same spot within 3 s, and 0 of 3 within 1.5 s. Exact 95% ranges if this recording is typical are 29.2-100.0% and 0.0-70.8% of crossings (Clopper-Pearson) and 0.6-8.8 and 0.0-3.7 people in a recording this long (Poisson).

There were 0 serious near-misses by the definition of pedestrian and moving vehicle on the same spot less than 1.5 s apart, and 3 close passes of 1.5-3.0 s.

The closest pass was a close pass with PET of 1.7 s involving a car at 51.0 km/h, with an adult death risk if hit of 5.8% (Rosén & Sander 2009, adults 15+, car fronts).
Another close pass had a PET of 1.6 s involving a motorcycle at 31.9 km/h, with an adult death risk if hit of 1.4%.
A third close pass had a PET of 1.8 s involving a bus at 21.9 km/h, with an adult death risk if hit of 0.3%.

For context, PV² and hourly rates need at least 15 minutes of video and this one is 7.3 minutes with 3 crossings and 6 moving vehicles, so rates from this short sample must be treated with caution. In this sample 96.5% of the time was inside gaps of 6 s or more with no moving vehicle where people crossed, with 11 such gaps and 5 of 12 s or more and longest 75.0 s, noting the first and last gaps are cut short by the video.

We request installation of a raised zebra crossing at this location to reduce vehicle speeds and give pedestrians priority.

We have the Crossing Watch video and tracking data using SAM road-plane geometry and post-encroachment time and are happy to share it.

Yours faithfully,
The Principal
